newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end mixed, then jump on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end mixed, then jump on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a moderate session, then jumped on ACCESS after an unexpectedly-huge draw in the weekly AGA storage report, industry sources said.
February eased 0.8 cent to close at $2.908 per million British thermal units, then jumped to $2.96 on ACCESS after the data. March settled 0.4 cent higher at $2.636.

"The (AGA) number is huge. It's the biggest draw we've ever seen," said one East Coast trader, adding short covering this afternoon helped lift the complex from early lows but mild weather was still likely to undermine sentiment.

AGA said late Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 262 bcf, well-above expectations, and were now 18 bcf below year-ago levels. Eastern storage fell by 151 bcf but was still 173 bcf, or 19 percent, above last year.
A Reuter poll showed traders expected a weekly AGA draw in the 190-195 bcf range.
But while the market was technically oversold and due for a short covering bounce, particularly with bullish AGA data, few saw much upside without another broad, Arctic air mass.
And most forecasters offered little hope for the bulls, expecting normal to above-normal temperatures to dominate the U.S. into early February.

Technically, traders pegged February support first in the $2.83-2.84 area and then at the December 31 low of $2.613. Psychological resistance was seen at $3.00, with better selling likely at $3.33, $3.64 and then $3.80-3.84.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained about five cents Wednesday to near the $3.00 level. Midcontinent pipes were steady to up slightly in the $2.85-2.90 range. New York city gate gas slipped 10-25 cents to the $3.20s and $3.30s on milder weather in the area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell by 1.2 cents to $2.283.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas expires next Monday.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Tuesday.

On the KCBT, February closed 4.5 cents lower at $2.745, while most deferreds finished down by one to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.7 cents to 16.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 1,194 contracts traded, up sharply from Tuesday's total of 419.
